To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SIM PlanetQuest YSO program will detect planets in the habitable zones of approximately 20–30 stars.

we have found a few YSOs in Taurus and Sco‐Cen that have radial velocity companions and that a large fraction of the stars are variable to some degree, but we have not found any stars that have common proper motion companions to within 140 AU.

we have identified several hundred YSOs that are good candidates for SIM PlanetQuest astrometry, and that the most important observable to determine whether a star is suitable for SIM PlanetQuest is photometric variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation and evolution of planetary systems around young stars, and we hope to provide the community with a list of stars for which SIM will be able to detect Jupiter‐mass companions.
the formation of planetary systems around young stars, and the results of the precursor observations will help us to understand the processes that govern the formation of planetary mass companions.
understanding the physical and chemical properties of the interstellar medium and its relation to star formation, and the evolution of the interstellar matter in the Galaxy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1) the YSO Key Project is a feasible program, 2) the targets in Taurus are the most promising, 3) the Pleiades targets are the least promising, and 4) the Sco‐Cen targets are in between.
the SIM Key Project will detect planets around YSOs, but only if the SIM astrometry is performed in a way to minimize the effects of photometric variability.
the SIM PlanetQuest YSO Key Project will be a very challenging but feasible project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a sample of YSOs that are free of common proper motion companions, have small photometric variability, and have no signs of a stellar or substellar companion in interferometric data.
approximately half of our YSOs are viable targets for SIM.
the SIM YSO Key Project is a viable program, but it requires a significant amount of work before it can be executed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SIM YSO Key Project will have to rely on a combination of astrometric, interferometric, and radial velocity measurements to determine the viability of the stars in the SIM YSO sample for the detection of Jupiter‐mass planets.
SIM will be able to detect gas giant planets in orbits of a few to a few tens of AU around young stars.
the YSO sample will require a significant amount of follow‐up work to ensure that the astrometric noise is minimized.
